Public domain: every person whose words are in this text died in 1925 or earlier, so the term has ended under the law of every country, whichever one first published it.

People: Dante Alighieri (author, Wikidata Q1067), died 1321; Gustave Doré (illustrator, Wikidata Q6682), died 1883; Henry Francis Cary (translator, Wikidata Q1961974), died 1844. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Dante Alighieri, 1265-1321; Doré, Gustave, 1832-1883 [Illustrator]; Cary, Henry Francis, 1772-1844 [Translator]") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's.

Printed edition: The Vision : or, Hell, Purgatory, and Paradise, of Dante Alighieri, New York : Thomas Y. Crowell, 1881, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/visionorhellpurg00dant. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 50%, 38%, 89% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of Gustave Doré, Henry Francis Cary, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
